summary:
**CHANGE (Comprehensive Historical Analysis of NASA Geospatial Evidence)** is an interactive Earth-system trend detective that lets anyone pick a place on Earth, a NASA climate variable, and a time period—then instantly computes whether a statistically significant trend exists, how fast it is changing per decade, and what the spatial pattern looks like on a satellite map.

The tool integrates three independent NASA data sources: POWER (MERRA-2) for 20+ surface/solar/soil variables (1981-present), GISTEMP v4 for global and zonal temperature anomalies (1880-present), and GES DISC gridded products via OPeNDAP. Ten curated regions (Svalbard, Greenland, Amazon, Sahel, Congo, Barrier Reef, California, Himalaya, Lake Chad, Alaska North Slope) provide documented Earth-system stories as starting points, while custom coordinates enable global exploration.

All statistics run client-side with zero dependencies: Mann-Kendall (tie-corrected) for significance at alpha=0.05, Theil-Sen (Gilbert 95% CI) for robust rate-of-change, and OLS with Student-t for comparison. A map time machine renders NASA GIBS monthly rasters at any historical month to visualize the spatial footprint behind the number. Every result exports as a reproducible CSV with full metadata, enabling transparent scrutiny of every claim.
details:
CHANGE is a browser-based Earth-system trend detective. The user selects a location (from ten curated regions or any custom coordinate), a NASA climate variable, and a time period. The app fetches live data from three independent NASA sources, computes three statistical tests entirely in the browser, and returns a one-sentence verdict with the rate of change per decade, significance level, and confidence interval. A synchronized map time machine then renders the corresponding NASA GIBS satellite raster for any historical month, revealing the spatial pattern behind the number. Every analysis exports as a reproducible CSV with full metadata and method documentation.

Benefits

  • Zero-barrier access: Runs in any browser, no account, no API keys for POWER and GISTEMP.
  • Statistical rigor: Mann–Kendall (tie-corrected) for significance, Theil–Sen (Gilbert CI) for robust slope, OLS for comparison—all dependency-free.
  • Multi-source triangulation: Three independent NASA datasets (POWER, GISTEMP, GES DISC) let users cross-check signals.
  • Transparent reproducibility: Every number is traceable to its source, method, and parameters; CSV export enables independent verification.
  • Spatial context: The GIBS time machine grounds abstract trends in visible planetary change.

Intended impact
Democratize NASA Earth observation data so students, journalists, policymakers, and citizens can independently detect and verify climate trends at any location—turning passive data consumption into active evidence-based exploration.

Tools, languages, hardware, software

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, Recharts, TanStack Query
  • Statistics engine: Pure TypeScript (no external deps)—Mann–Kendall, Theil–Sen, OLS with Student-t and normal distributions
  • NASA data clients: POWER JSON, GISTEMP CSV (proxied via Cloudflare Functions to bypass CORS), GES DISC OPeNDAP (server-side token)
  • Deployment: Cloudflare Pages + Cloudflare Pages Functions (edge caching, CORS proxy, secret management)
  • Development: Node.js, pnpm, oxlint, wrangler CLI
  • Hardware: Standard laptop; no specialized hardware required.

Creativity

  • Unified three-source architecture with a single control panel (place → variable → period) that abstracts away each dataset’s quirks.
  • Verdict-first UI: The statistical conclusion is a readable sentence, not a table—designed for human judgment, not just analysis.
  • Map time machine binds the chart to the planet: sliding the year/month rewinds the satellite view to the exact month the trend summarizes.
  • Honesty defaults: GIBS dates clamped to real product coverage; ocean points labelled as reanalysis; gaps dropped not zero-filled; anomaly mode uses WMO 1991–2020 baseline.

Factors considered

  • CORS & throttling: GISTEMP blocked in-browser; solved with a cached Cloudflare Function proxy.
  • Credential safety: Earthdata tokens never touch the browser; server-side attachment in a locked-down Function.
  • Statistical transparency: All three tests shown, with Mann–Kendall as the reference verdict; OLS flagged as fragile.
  • Offline reproducibility: Engine is pure TypeScript—runs identically in Node (scripts/results.ts) for published-number verification.
  • Performance: Client-side stats on ~500 monthly points complete in <50 ms; GIBS tiles cached at edge.
  • Accessibility: Semantic HTML, keyboard-navigable controls, high-contrast chart colors, responsive layout down to mobile.
